book.title: 30 Years, No Power
book.subtitle: The Visual, Fact-Checked Survival Field Manual
book.tagline: For families, babies, women, dogs and everyone who has to keep living when the grid does not come back.

critical.label: Critical
critical.meaning: Can save a life in minutes to days. Learn first.

core.label: Core
core.meaning: Needed to get through months and years.

long.label: Long haul
long.meaning: Needed to keep going for 30 years and rebuild.

parts.title: Start Here
parts.intro: What this book is, how to use it in a crisis, and the exact order of actions for the first 72 hours, the first month and the next 30 years.

parts.title: Mind & Plan
parts.intro: How people actually behave in disasters, how to plan as a family or group, and how to decide whether to stay or go.

parts.title: Water
parts.intro: A person dies of dehydration long before starvation. How much water you need, how to store it, find it, and make it safe for decades.

parts.title: Food
parts.intro: Storing food that lasts, cooking without power, preserving harvests, growing staple calories, foraging safely, hunting, fishing and raising animals.

parts.title: Medicine & First Aid
parts.intro: First aid that saves lives in minutes, treating injuries and infections when no hospital is coming, and keeping medicines working for as long as possible.

parts.title: Women's & Girls' Health
parts.intro: Periods, contraception, pregnancy, emergency childbirth, recovery after birth, breastfeeding and personal safety for women and girls.

parts.title: Babies & Children
parts.intro: Keeping newborns, babies and children alive and healthy: feeding, warmth, hygiene, danger signs, safety, education and emotional health.

parts.title: Dogs & Animals
parts.intro: Dogs as guards, helpers and family. Feeding them without kibble, keeping them healthy, first aid, training, breeding, plus cats, livestock and draft animals.

parts.title: Shelter, Heat & Light
parts.intro: Staying warm, cool, dry and lit without electricity, and doing it without poisoning yourself with carbon monoxide or burning the house down.

parts.title: Tools & Skills
parts.intro: The hand tools that matter, keeping them working for decades, and the core trades: rope, wood, metal, sewing, soap and low-tech chemistry.

parts.title: Hygiene & Sanitation
parts.intro: Clean hands, safe toilets and pest control prevent more deaths than almost anything else after a disaster.

parts.title: Security & Community
parts.intro: Staying safe through deterrence, a low profile, de-escalation and strong neighbors, plus trade, group rules and safe firearm storage.

parts.title: Scavenging & Salvage
parts.intro: Finding and reusing what is left lawfully and safely: what to look for first, what is still usable, and the hazards that injure scavengers.

parts.title: Navigation, Comms & Travel
parts.intro: Finding your way, talking over distance without the internet, signaling for help, keeping time and records, and moving people and loads.

parts.title: Disasters & Hazards
parts.intro: What the evidence says about each major hazard, from winter storms and floods to radiation, pandemics and solar storms.

parts.title: The 30-Year Plan
parts.intro: Lessons from real long blackouts and sieges, and a phased plan to feed, heal, teach and govern a community for three decades.

parts.title: Reference
parts.intro: Master checklists, shelf-life tables, conversions and a glossary to keep at hand.
